chapter: Childhood in Oklahoma, Kansas City and Tulsa
title: Tulsa schools and the Army-sergeant bandmaster William Jett
summary: Names his Tulsa schools and praises his baritone-playing bandmaster William Jett.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: What was the name of the high school you want to (in Tulsa)?
In Tulsa, Booker T. Washington High. [George Washington] Then I went to Carver Junior High. That's the same year he
was, you know, acclaimed for the peanut. And they started naming schools after him. And then I went back to Booker T. High, to high school.
And that was a high school band you were in when you marched past Sousa?

Yeah. And my bandmaster was out of sight. He played baritone horn. He was a sergeant in the Army. And he had charge of the band, also. And he had the most beautiful tone on the baritone you have ever heard. And he could play it and you could hear him for almost two miles. He's here, now, but he's a reverend. He gave up music. He had a bad thing to happen to him domestically in Oklahoma. He quit the band and left. And joined the church.
